questions.stem: What is the equation for gravitational potential energy?
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy is calculated using GPE = mgh, where m is mass (kg), g is gravitational field strength (N/kg), and h is height (m).

questions.stem: Calculate the GPE of a 5 kg object held 10 m above the ground (g = 10 N/kg).
If an object is raised to twice its original height, its GPE will:
questions.explanation: GPE is directly proportional to height (GPE = mgh). Doubling the height doubles the gravitational potential energy.

questions.stem: When an object falls freely (no air resistance), its GPE is converted into:
questions.explanation: When an object falls without air resistance, gravitational potential energy is converted directly into kinetic energy. The total energy remains constant.

questions.stem: An object has 2000 J of GPE and a mass of 10 kg. If g = 10 N/kg, what height is it at?
Which factor does NOT affect the gravitational potential energy of an object?
questions.explanation: GPE = mgh depends on mass, gravitational field strength, and height. Speed does not affect GPE -- speed relates to kinetic energy instead.

questions.stem: Why does the same object have less GPE on the Moon than on Earth at the same height?

options.text: Because the object has less mass on the Moon
Because height is measured differently on the Moon
Because there is no atmosphere on the Moon
Because the Moon has a weaker gravitational field strength

questions.explanation: GPE = mgh. The Moon has a weaker gravitational field strength (g = 1.6 N/kg vs 9.8 N/kg on Earth), so GPE is less for the same mass and height.
